summary: Ra is a tense bidding game where players use a shrinking pool of numbered sun tiles to win auctions for tiles that score points immediately, protect against penalties, or pay off at the end of an epoch. The game's signature tension comes from the Ra tile forcing early epoch endings and from the escalating temptation to keep drawing tiles into an auction rather than triggering one yourself.
praised: Fast to teach and play despite meaningful depth
Every sun tile bid is a genuine dilemma with opportunity cost
Scales well and plays quickly across its full 2-5 player range
criticised: Heavy luck in tile draws can swing a game regardless of skill
Endgame scoring math (especially civilizations and monuments) can feel fiddly for new players
Downtime during other players' auctions in higher player counts
Some find the theme pasted-on rather than integrated

scoring.why: Final score comes from a mix of gold, civilization sets, monuments, Pharaoh/Nile/flood tiles, and end-game bonuses/penalties, so winning requires balancing several scoring tracks rather than maximizing one.
